Works with

Rugged tablet for Gas Engineer Software

Gas Engineer Software, often shortened to GES, is job management and certificate software for UK heating and plumbing businesses. It is built and sold by Software Works for You Ltd, a UK company whose site says it has offices in Sevenoaks and London; Companies House lists Software Works For You Limited, company number 08306248, incorporated in 2012. The vendor describes the product as digital records and certificates, job sheets, scheduling, quotes, invoices, payments and automatic service reminders, with a web portal for the office and native iOS and Android apps for engineers that share the same data.

The app is where the site work happens. The vendor's help centre says the app is more commonly used to create certificates in the field, and its Google Play listing describes gas, oil and heat pump certificates signed on site and sent, photos added to records, readings pulled from a Bluetooth flue gas analyser straight into a certificate, and full offline access on the mobile apps with syncing when next online. That is a device that goes into airing cupboards, lofts, plant rooms and cellars, rides in a van between jobs and gets handed to a customer to sign, which is where a consumer tablet with no sealing or drop rating tends to have a short life. This page does not cover what any certificate or record must contain; the software produces digital certificates, and you should check the records your business needs on the device before you rely on it.

This page sets out what Gas Engineer Software publishes about the devices its app runs on, which Tuga rugged tablets meet those published requirements, where the Windows option fits and where it does not, and how a sole trader or small firm can buy a single unit to try before kitting out a team.

Requirements

What Gas Engineer Software needs from a device

Each item below comes from Software Works for You Ltd (trading as Gas Engineer Software)'s own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android 11 or higher, on tablets and phones

    The vendor's help centre article Which devices does Gas Engineer Software support (dated 17 July 2026) states that Android tablets and phones are supported through the app and the website and require OS version 11 or higher. For Apple devices it gives iOS 13 or higher, though the App Store listing itself currently says iOS 15.0 or later. It lists Huawei and Honor mobile devices as unsupported. No RAM, storage, processor or screen-size figure is published for any mobile device. Source: help.gasengineersoftware.co.uk

  • Android app from Google Play, for phones and tablets

    The Android app is published on Google Play as Gas Engineer Software - GES (package com.gasengineerapp, developer Software Works for You Ltd). When checked on 19 October 2026 the listing showed version 6.93, updated 15 October 2026, with a minimum API level of 30 (Android 11), which matches the help centre figure, and device chips for Phone and Tablet. The listing describes the app as working on your phone or back at the office, and the vendor's site links to Google Play for the Android download. Source: play.google.com

  • Offline working once logged in, with periodic syncing on the apps

    The devices article says you can use the apps without an internet connection once you are logged in, and that without a connection anything you do will be unable to sync to other devices. The Google Play listing describes full offline access on the mobile apps, syncing when next online, and the vendor's records page says offline drafts auto-save to the device and sync when back online. The sync article says the web portal syncs constantly in the background while the mobile apps sync periodically because they are designed to operate offline and online, and that a Sync Data Now button on the home page forces a sync. The vendor does not publish how much data is held on the device. Source: help.gasengineersoftware.co.uk

  • Photos from the camera or library, attached to records, jobs and emails

    The help centre's photos article (dated 17 July 2026) says that on the mobile app you can add a photo while creating a record by tapping the camera icon, taking a new photo with the camera or choosing one from the library. Photos saved against a job are attached automatically when a record or certificate is emailed unless marked for your own reference, and a paperclip icon on the email screen adds further attachments. The vendor says not every image format is supported and recommends a standard format such as JPEG or PNG. On the web portal, photos are uploaded to a job through a Photos button. Source: help.gasengineersoftware.co.uk

  • Certificates signed on screen in the app

    The help centre's certificate article says you fill out a record until you reach the signature screen, where you can Save it, return Home or Approve it; saved records stay in the app and approved records can still be edited later. The vendor's records page says you get the customer's signature on your phone, tap approve, and the customer receives the certificate by email, with a Sign below to approve prompt on the signing screen. All certificates can also be created on the web portal. The vendor publishes no stylus or screen-size requirement for signing. Source: help.gasengineersoftware.co.uk

  • Bluetooth for flue gas analyser readings, in the app only

    The help centre's flue gas analyser article (dated 17 July 2026) says the integration works with Bluetooth-enabled analysers and pulls readings directly into the app, that Bluetooth must be enabled on the mobile device, and that older analyser models may not have Bluetooth. It lists Anton Sprint Pro3 and above, Kane KANE258, KANE358, KANE458 and KANE458s, and TPI DC710 and DC711. The integration is described in the app only; the article does not mention the web portal. The only scanning the vendor mentions is a line on its records page about scanning serial numbers, with no method published; no barcode or QR code scanning by the device, dedicated scan engine, external scanner or NFC is documented. The QR codes the vendor describes are payment codes on invoices that the customer scans with their own phone. Source: help.gasengineersoftware.co.uk

  • Windows: no Windows app, website access in a browser

    The devices article lists Windows desktops and laptops as supported for website access only, and macOS 11 or higher for website access. No native Windows app is published, and the vendor does not publish a browser list or browser version numbers. Help centre articles refer to the web portal in Chrome and Safari in passing (a black screen when viewing a PDF in Chrome, and exported files not displaying in Safari), but neither is stated as a requirement. The offline working, signature screen, camera photos and flue gas analyser integration the vendor documents are features of the mobile app. Source: help.gasengineersoftware.co.uk

Setting up

Getting Gas Engineer Software running

  1. Start a Gas Engineer Software account at gasengineersoftware.co.uk, or ask the account owner to add the engineer as a user. The vendor offers a 14 day free trial with no card required.
  2. On the Tuga A10, A8 or A6, open Google Play and install Gas Engineer Software - GES (package com.gasengineerapp, developer Software Works for You Ltd), then sign in with the engineer's email address and password.
  3. While the device is online, tap Sync Data Now on the app's home page so customers, job addresses and records are on the device before the first job without signal. The vendor says you can use the app without a connection once logged in, but nothing done offline reaches other devices until the next sync.
  4. Allow camera access when the app asks, so the camera icon on a record can take a photo without leaving the screen. Keep photos in a standard format such as JPEG or PNG, as the vendor recommends.
  5. If you use an Anton, Kane or TPI flue gas analyser from the vendor's compatible list, switch on Bluetooth on the tablet and pair the analyser following the vendor's flue gas analyser article, then check readings land in a test record.
  6. Complete a test record end to end on the device: fill it in, reach the signature screen, sign and tap Approve, and check the emailed PDF and attached photos look right, before rolling out to the team.
  7. On a Tuga W10, open the web portal in Edge or Chrome and keep the browser updated. Use it for office work; it will not run the mobile app, and the vendor documents offline working on the apps only.
  8. For the A10 and A8, fit the vehicle mounting dock in the van; for the A10 and W10, add the charging dock where devices live overnight; for the A6, add the belt holster. Fit the tempered glass screen protector before the device goes out.

Questions

Gas Engineer Software on a Tuga device

Gas Engineer Software publishes a requirement of Android 11 or higher for tablets and phones, and its Google Play listing gives a minimum API level of 30 (Android 11). The Tuga A10 runs Android 14 with Google Play, so it meets the published figure, as do the Tuga A8 (Android 12) and the Tuga A6 (Android 15). The vendor publishes no RAM or storage figure for mobile devices and lists only Huawei and Honor devices as unsupported. We do not describe any device as certified or tested by Gas Engineer Software; these are the vendor's published requirements set against the device specifications, so try the app on one unit before buying for a team.

The vendor says you can use the apps without an internet connection once you are logged in, that offline drafts auto-save to the device and sync when back online, and that the mobile apps sync periodically with a Sync Data Now button to force one. Anything done offline cannot reach other devices until the next sync, so sync before leaving a property with no signal if the office needs to see the record straight away. The A10, A8 and A6 all run the Google Play app. A Tuga W10 can only use the web portal in a browser, and the vendor does not document offline working there.

Yes. The vendor's certificate article describes filling out a record until you reach the signature screen, then saving or approving it, and its records page says you get the customer's signature on your phone and tap approve to email the certificate. The vendor publishes no stylus requirement, so a finger is fine. We sell a capacitive stylus for the A8, A10 and W10 at £14.99; it is not listed as compatible with the A6. The software produces the digital certificate; check the records your business uses on the device rather than relying on this page for what they contain.

The vendor's integration works over Bluetooth with the analysers on its compatible list (Anton Sprint Pro3 and above, Kane KANE258, KANE358, KANE458 and KANE458s, and TPI DC710 and DC711), in the app only, with Bluetooth switched on at the device. The A10 (Bluetooth 5.2), A8 (Bluetooth) and A6 (Bluetooth 5.1) all have it. The vendor documents no barcode or QR scanning by the device, so the A6's Zebra 2D scan engine is not a Gas Engineer Software input, and the only scanning the vendor mentions is a line about scanning serial numbers with no method published.

Both meet the published Android 11 requirement. The A10 has more RAM (8GB against 6GB), a sharper 1920 x 1200 screen for long records and a larger signature box, IP68 against IP67, and MIL-STD-810H, which the A8 does not have. The A8 has a 1000 nit screen against the A10's 350 nits, a removable battery, VESA mount points, and costs £379 against £449. Engineers who read the screen outside at the meter or the oil tank, or who want one-handed use in tight spaces, may prefer the A8; those filling in long records in wetter or harder conditions are better served by the A10.
